Hyperliquid launched it's token 2 years ago, the airdrop was a life changing event for many, myself included. It was the vindication of a thesis @SoskaKyle and I had had for a long time. Perpetual swaps are going to be the dominant retail product in finance for the next decade.

Performance wise, the market has continued to reward this thesis. Every other attempt at utilizing blockchain technology to create something of value has been a spectacular failure. 

If you're in crypto and you do not use Hyperliquid, I question why you spend time in this industry at all. If you're still holding any other altcoins, you're a fundamentally unserious investor. Crypto traders have a very hard to thinking about actual fundamentals, because crypto has had an absence of it for so long. 

Crypto traders cannot mentally model compounding, most people are geared towards momentum, look at memecoins. A lot of people feel like they're too late because Hype is now trading a $60 and that they "won't make it". They then go to own more speculative, lower quality alternatives while they miss out on the steady compounding that a fundamentally strong asset provides. 

Crypto traders consistently miss an obvious fact, if Hype going from $60 to some much higher price is likely, but you feel that it does not make a material difference to your portfolio then leverage is always at your disposal. You're getting a strictly worse risk/reward by attempting to long "beta" plays in lesser quality assets. Just own more of the market leader.

The best time to sell all your altcoins for Hype was Thanksgiving 2024. The second best time is today.

If you care about crypto, you must use the products.

tweets.text:
Most useful thing for me has been understanding what i actually want up front. Which has meant defining it first (and more importantly what it isn't) on paper, reviewing it, then moving to prompting

If i know a general direction/outcome, i find telling it the things I don't want in detail, more valuable than what i do want. This way the hallucinatory creep it goes on where it begins using its own work as assumptions on what you want are at least directionally correct

Investors are piling into leveraged semiconductor trades:

The 3x leveraged long semiconductor ETF, SOXL, has attracted +$1.9 billion in inflows so far this week.

On Monday alone, the fund recorded +$1.7 billion in inflows, its largest daily intake since November 6th.

This follows +$2.7 billion in inflows during the previous week, its 3rd-largest weekly intake since June.

Meanwhile, over the 20 trading days ended Friday, retail net purchases of SOXL rose to +$1.3 billion, the largest 20-day rolling sum since at least December 2024.

Furthermore, the semiconductor ETF, SMH, has attracted +$2.9 billion in inflows so far in November, on track for its biggest monthly intake since July and 3rd-largest since May 2023.

Investors are buying the dip in chip stocks on leverage.
